prompt: Which correctly defines an abstract class Vehicle with an abstract method fuelType()?
choices: abstract class Vehicle { abstract String fuelType(); }
abstract class Vehicle { String fuelType() { return ""; } }
explanation: abstract class + abstract method: the method has no body; subclasses must implement it. Option A is an interface, not an abstract class. Option C is a concrete class — its fuelType() has an empty body but CAN be overridden. Option D has a body — it's a concrete method inside an abstract class (legal but not abstract).
